title: SA/164/2014 of Fateh Singh Panwar AND OTHERS Vs Vijay Chand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Second Appeal No. 164 of 2014

Fateh Singh Panwar and others. ..Ö..Appellants.
Versus
Vijay Chand
and others. ..Ö..Respondents.

Present:
Mr. Ravi Babulkar, Advocate for Appellants.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral)
Present second appeal is preferred assailing the
judgment and decree dated 12.10.2009 passed by Civil Judge
(SD), Uttarkashi whereby Civil Suit No. 28 of 2008 (Fateh Singh
Panwar Vs. Vijay Chand) was dismissed as well as judgment
and decree dated 18.09.2014 passed by District Judge,
Uttarkashi whereby first Civil Appeal No. 17 of 2009 was also
dismissed upholding the judgment and decree dated
12.10.2009.
Brief facts of the present case, inter alia, are that few
villagers of village Sald filed O.S. No. 28 of 2008 in the court of
Civil Judge (SD) Uttarkashi against the villagers of village
Kharwa, Patti Barsali, Tehsil Dunda, District Uttarkashi for the
mandatory injunction seeking direction to the defendants to
dislodge the idol of Asht Bhuja Goddess Durga from temple of
village Kharwa and reinstalled the same in village Sald with the
allegation that idol of Goddess Durga was earlier installed in
an old temple of village Sald; in the year 1984, villagers decided
to renovate / reconstruct the old temple of Goddess Durga and
it was decided that during the period of renovation /
reconstruction of the temple of Goddess Durga in village Sald,

2
idol of Goddess Durga would be shifted and installed
temporarily in the temple of village Kharwa; therefore, under
the agreement between the villagers of both the villages, idol of
Goddess Durga was shifted from village Sald to village
Kharwa; and in the temple of village Kharwa, after performing
of rituals of Pran Prathista, idol of Goddess Durga was
installed; renovation / reconstruction work of temple at village
Sald was completed in the year 1991; thereafter, a demand was
raised by the villagers of village Sald to shift back the idol of
Goddess Durga from village Kharwa to village Sald; however,
few priests and elders opined that idol of Goddess Durga
should not be shifted before expiry of 12 years and it was
agreed that after expiry of 12 years idol of Goddess Durga
would be reinstalled in the temple of village Sald, however,
later on, villagers of village Kharwa refused to return the idol of
Goddess Durga to be reinstalled in temple of village Sald,
therefore, cause of action arose for the present suit.
Defendant appeared and preferred their written
statement saying idol of Goddess Durga, which is available in
the temple of village Kharwa, was installed about 60 years
before and it was never dislodged from any temple of village
Sald.
Suit was permitted to be filed in the representative
capacity under Order 1 Rule 8 CPC. Having considered the
pleadings of both the parties and evidence available on record
learned trial court was pleased to record finding of fact that
plaintiffs have failed to prove that earlier idol of Goddess
Durga (subject matter of the suit) was installed in the old
temple of village Sald. It has further been observed by the
learned trial Judge that plaintiffs, by producing any resolution
for reconstruction / renovation of the temple, could have easily

3
proved that under such and such resolution, temple was
decided to be renovated and accordingly, renovated; under
such and such resolution, it was resolved that idol of Goddess
Durga would be shifted and remain installed in temple of
village Kharwa. Learned trial court has further observed that
no Priest or eyewitness was produced, who could say that in
fact, he was the priest, who has uprooted the idol of Goddess
Durga from temple of village Sald and has installed, after doing
Pran Prathista, in village Kharwa or in his presence idol was
uprooted from village Sald and was reinstalled in village
Kharwa.
Suit was ultimately dismissed by the trial court vide
judgment and decree dated 12.10.2009. Feeling aggrieved,
plaintiffs have preferred first appeal being First Civil Appeal
No. 17 of 2009 before District Judge, Uttarkashi. However,
appeal was also dismissed by the first appellate Court and
findings recorded by the trial court was confirmed.
As per Section 100 of CPC, second appeal can be
entertained by this Court, if this Court is satisfied that case
involves substantial question(s) of law.
Let me now examine as to whether, present appeal
involves any substantial question of law, which requires
adjudication by this Court.
In the present case, it was the duty of the plaintiffs /
appellants, herein, to prove that earlier idol of Goddess Durga
(subject matter of the suit) was installed in the temple of village
Sald and under such and such resolution, villagers or the
Management Committee of the temple decided to renovate the
old dilapidated temple and to shift the idol meanwhile to
village Kharwa. However, neither such resolution is placed nor

4
any other evidence is placed on record that when such
resolution was passed and by whom. Not only this, no priest or
any other evidence was produced whereby it could be said that
on such and such date idol of Goddess Durga was uprooted
from temple of village Sald and reinstalled in temple of village
Kharwa after performing the rituals / ceremony of Pran
Prathista. Not only this, none of the witnesses produced by the
plaintiffs has stated that he was present at the time of uprooting
or reinstalling of idol.
In my humble opinion, present case revolves
around the factual controversy and concurrent findings of fact
have already been recorded by the courts below. Since, in the
present case only question of fact is involved, which has
already been dealt with and decided by courts below, therefore,
in my humble opinion, no substantial question of law seems to
have arisen in the present case. Therefore, I do not find any
reason or justification to entertain this second appeal.
Consequently, appeal fails and is hereby dismissed in limine.
No order as to costs.
CLMA No. 14401 of 2014 stands disposed of
accordingly.
 (Alok Singh, J.)
 18.12.2014
SKS
